analyst_note: Hormuz Day 84; Naval Blockade Day 41; Project Freedom Pause Day 17; WPA Day 23 Past Statutory Deadline / 7 Days to 90-Day Hard Deadline May 29; Warsh Day 8. Friday May 22, 2026 opens on three overnight developments that structurally shift the situational picture from the May 21 morning brief. The primary new development is domestic and constitutional: House Republican leadership canceled a scheduled Iran war powers resolution vote on the afternoon of May 21, after a procedural vote on the Smithsonian American Women's History Museum construction bill revealed eight Republican absences and six Republicans voting with Democrats — a majority coalition signal that forced the pull. Rep. Jared Golden (D-Maine) — the one consistent Democratic holdout against every prior Iran war powers vote — confirmed he was prepared to flip yes, removing the final structural obstacle to passage. Rep. Gregory Meeks (D-NY), the resolution's sponsor, stated plainly: 'No question about it, we would have succeeded.' The House GOP leadership pulled the vote rather than absorb a bipartisan rebuke of presidential war-making. The next House attempt is now projected for early June, after the Memorial Day recess (active through May 26). This timing is constitutionally significant: the WPA 90-day hard deadline arrives May 29 — seven days from today — which falls inside the recess window. The next House vote comes after that deadline. The legal architecture changes fundamentally at Day 90: the administration's 'hostilities terminated' posture — asserting the ceasefire pause stopped the 60-day WPA clock — does not survive at Day 90 under any credible legal theory, including its own. The plain-text 90-day provision requires cessation of hostilities or congressional authorization. Neither exists. The second overnight development is the most significant deal-track structural shift since the May 6 Axios MOU scoop: third-party reporting now establishes that the actual negotiating range on the uranium enrichment moratorium duration is 12-15 years — specifically, at least 12 years with 15 as the likely landing spot — a 3-year negotiating margin rather than the 15-year gap implied by the public framing of Iran's 5-year offer against the US 20-year demand. This convergence is structurally meaningful and implies that prior 'unbridgeable gap' characterizations reflected public posturing rather than the operational negotiating range. However, the convergence on duration does not resolve the categorical distinction in Steve Witkoff's public demand: Witkoff has insisted on dismantlement of Iran's enrichment facilities at Natanz, Fordow, and Isfahan — not a moratorium of any duration — and dismantlement is categorically different from a 12-15-year moratorium followed by resumed 3.67% enrichment. Separately, Trump has reportedly softened on whether Iran must surrender its entire highly enriched uranium stockpile, introducing a further flip-flop with significant implications for the congressional zero-enrichment constraint (52 senators, 177 House members). The third development: Pakistan's Army Chief is traveling to Tehran for direct engagement, representing the most substantive escalation of the Pakistan mediation channel since Vice President Vance's Islamabad visit in April. On the economic front, Kevin Warsh enters Day 8 of his Federal Reserve chairmanship without a public statement, and the 30-year Treasury yield has now climbed to 5.18% — the highest level since 2007, per US News — while a new piece published this morning by US News and World Report is headlined 'Warsh Takes Over Fed With a Policy Problem Already in View.' The article flags the compounding pressure of supply-shock energy inflation, AI-driven capital demand, and fiscal deficits on a bond market that is pricing an increasingly aggressive rate trajectory under the new chair. The Motley Fool's 'Seven Words' analysis (May 20) on Warsh's balance-sheet ideology — 'the Fed must stay in its lane' as a preference for quantitative tightening — continues to circulate; QT in a 5.18% 30-year environment would compound fiscal and mortgage market stress simultaneously. Memorial Day recess closes federal legislative channels through May 26 — one day before the WPA 90-day hard deadline. Vibe 3: the deal track has more visible structural convergence than at any point since the Axios scoop, the bipartisan House coalition against unauthorized war is demonstrably real, and Trump's patience signal is an anti-escalation marker. Against these, the May 29 deadline is the most consequential domestic legal milestone of the conflict cycle; it arrives during a recess with no vote scheduled; Witkoff's dismantlement demand and the congressional zero-enrichment constraint remain structurally operative; Warsh is at Day 8 of the deepest Fed communication vacuum of the modern era; and the Oregon fire season structural stack is the most severe of the current cycle. Vibe 3.

vibe.rationale: Vibe 3. Three overnight developments drive the morning assessment. The case for moving above 3 (toward 4): the moratorium duration negotiating range has collapsed from a 15-year gap (5 vs. 20) to a 3-year margin (12-15), which represents the most significant structural convergence on the primary nuclear sticking point since negotiations began; Trump's patience signal ('willing to wait a few days') is a revealed anti-escalation preference, consistent with the May 19 strike hold; Pakistan's Army Chief traveling to Tehran represents the most substantive direct diplomatic escalation of the mediation channel since April, adding a new operational channel; and the House war powers vote cancellation demonstrates that the bipartisan coalition against unauthorized war is majority-capable, which — paradoxically — creates an accountability infrastructure that constrains the administration's maximalist postures. The case for staying at 3 rather than moving below: the deal track is alive; the moratorium convergence is real even if unconfirmed by bilateral statement; Trump has not issued a resumption order; war is not escalating today. The case against moving above 3: Witkoff's public dismantlement demand (Natanz, Fordow, Isfahan) is categorically different from a moratorium and remains unresolved by duration convergence alone; the congressional zero-enrichment constraint (52 senators, 177 House members) does not accept a moratorium of any duration — it requires zero enrichment, and a 12-15-year moratorium with resumed enrichment after expiry does not satisfy it; the WPA 90-day hard deadline is 7 days out with no vote scheduled, no congressional authorization obtained, and the next House attempt arriving after the deadline; Warsh is at Day 8 of the deepest modern-era Fed communication gap with the 30-year at 5.18% (2007 high); the Oregon fire season structural stack — 82% statewide drought, extreme Southern Cascades, 10-day prepositioning window, 15 days no federal response — is the worst entry condition of the current cycle. Net: Vibe 3. The deal track has converged materially on duration without resolving the categorical dismantlement-vs.-moratorium obstacle; the constitutional clock is working against every structural positive; and the PNW fire and economic threads are all moving in the wrong direction on calendar. Vibe 3 is a marginal holding position: genuine deal-track convergence plus genuine constitutional accountability pressure plus genuine fire season urgency, all unresolved.

items.headline: Moratorium Range Converges to 12-15 Years — 3-Year Margin vs. Prior 15-Year Gap; Witkoff Dismantlement Demand Still Maximalist; Trump Patience Signal; Pakistan Army Chief to Tehran; Hormuz Day 84
items.summary: The most significant overnight development on the deal track is the structural convergence of the uranium enrichment moratorium duration. Reporting from multiple third-party outlets now establishes that the actual negotiating range is 'at least 12 years' with '15 years as a likely landing spot' — a 3-year negotiating margin (12-15) rather than the 15-year gap implied by the public framing of Iran's 5-year offer against the US 20-year demand. Three sources cite 12 years as the floor and one puts 15 as the likely endpoint. Under the current MOU framework, Iran would be able to enrich uranium at low levels (3.67%) after the moratorium expires. This convergence is structurally significant: it suggests that the prior characterizations of an 'unbridgeable gap' reflected public posturing rather than operational negotiating range, and it establishes for the first time a credible middle ground on duration. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson confirmed May 21 that Tehran has received the latest US proposal and is reviewing it — the first formal acknowledgment of receipt since Trump's 'few more days' patience signal. Trump told CNBC on May 21 that he is 'willing to wait a few days' — the revealed patience preference consistent with the May 19 strike hold at Gulf allies' request and with the documented pattern ABC News has characterized as 'Trump's series of unenforced deadlines.' Pakistan's Army Chief is traveling to Tehran for direct engagement — the most substantive escalation of the Pakistan mediation channel since Vice President Vance's Islamabad visit in April. Pakistan has served as the primary indirect communications channel alongside Oman throughout the negotiation cycle; direct Army Chief engagement with Iranian leadership represents a qualitative escalation of that channel's operational weight. Critical structural caveat: Steve Witkoff's public demand remains at the maximalist end of the possible US position spectrum. Witkoff has publicly insisted that Iran's enrichment facilities at Natanz, Fordow, and Isfahan must be dismantled — not merely suspended or placed under a moratorium. Dismantlement is categorically different from a 12-15-year moratorium followed by resumed enrichment: it would require physical destruction of centrifuge cascades, removal of enriched uranium stockpiles, and IAEA verification of permanent cessation — a set of conditions Iran has explicitly and repeatedly rejected. The moratorium duration convergence does not resolve the dismantlement-vs.-moratorium categorical distinction. Separately, reporting indicates Trump may have softened his position on whether Iran must surrender its full highly enriched uranium stockpile — a potential flip-flop with significant implications for the congressional zero-enrichment constraint (52 senators, 177 House members on record), which requires both zero enrichment and HEU surrender. If Trump accepts a deal that includes continued enrichment under a 12-15-year moratorium, the zero-enrichment signatories face a choice between opposing a deal their president supports or accepting terms that contradict their stated position. The MOU 30-day framework structure remains operative: any deal would declare war's end and open a 30-day negotiation window on Hormuz transit, nuclear limits, and sanctions relief. Brent crude holds at approximately $106.92 and WTI at approximately $100.59 — slightly off from peak Hormuz Day 82 levels but sustained above the $100 threshold reflecting continued strait closure. Approximately 1,600 ships and 23,000 sailors remain stranded. Cumulative war cost last confirmed at $29 billion. Watch for: Araghchi or Pezeshkian statement specifically engaging the 12-15-year range; Witkoff clarification on dismantlement vs. moratorium distinction; Pakistan Army Chief Tehran talks outcome; Oman FM; any CENTCOM carrier positioning signal; Truth Social.

items.summary: Kevin Warsh enters Day 8 as Federal Reserve Chair without a public statement — the second consecutive week of the deepest modern-era Fed communication gap of any chair transition in the inflation-targeting era. The 30-year Treasury yield has now climbed to 5.18% per US News and World Report, the highest level since 2007 — a new high watermark for the conflict-cycle bond stress trajectory, above the approximately 5.121% reported in the May 21 morning brief. US News published a piece this morning — 'Warsh Takes Over Fed With a Policy Problem Already in View' — characterizing the economic inheritance: inflation running at 3.8% CPI YoY (April), approximately twice the Fed's 2% target; Brent oil above $100 driven by the US-Israeli war with Iran; high import tariffs compounding supply-shock pressure; utility and AI-infrastructure costs rising independently of the conflict. The article confirms the 30-year at 5.18% as the bond market's verdict on the policy gap. The Motley Fool's 'Seven Words' analysis (May 20) — framing Warsh's 'the Fed must stay in its lane' as a preference for selling down the Fed's $6.7 trillion balance sheet — continues to circulate; if Warsh moves toward quantitative tightening in a 5.18% 30-year environment, the compounding effects on fiscal sustainability (rising debt service on the $36+ trillion national debt), mortgage markets (30-year fixed rates would rise further), and municipal bond issuers (Portland's $172 million shortfall under current conditions) would represent the most consequential domestic financial stress cascade of the conflict cycle. April CPI at 3.8% YoY (three-year high), Core CPI at 2.8%, and PPI at 6.0% annually (against 4.9% consensus) provide no cover for a dovish interpretation of the inflation trajectory. Yardeni Research told CNBC on May 18 that the Fed may need to raise interest rates in July to appease bond vigilantes; the CME FedWatch June FOMC hold probability remains near 98%, but the July and December hike probabilities reflect increasing market pricing of a hawkish turn. The Shiller PE is approximately 41.83 against the dot-com record of 44.19 — equity valuations remain historically elevated against a fiscal and energy-cost backdrop that does not support the earnings trajectory implied by current prices. June FOMC is 26 days out; no Warsh public statement has been issued to anchor market interpretation of the Fed's reaction function. Day 8 is not stabilization — it is the compounding consequence of the deepest central bank communication vacuum in the inflation-targeting era, measured against a bond market that is pricing an increasingly aggressive rate path in the absence of any Fed guidance.

items.summary: Three domestic secondary threads. First: Warsh Day 8 — the Federal Reserve Chair has now been in office for a full work-week plus without a single public statement. The 30-year Treasury yield has climbed to 5.18%, the highest since 2007 per US News, while the 10-year holds at approximately 4.595%. The Motley Fool's 'Seven Words' balance sheet ideology piece (May 20) has circulated widely through this week; any Warsh public communication would be the most consequential domestic economic catalyst of the current cycle. The Yardeni July hike scenario (CNBC May 18) remains active; June FOMC is 26 days out with approximately 98% hold probability but with December hike odds elevated. Second: OHA measles enters 30 days of staleness on Friday May 22 — Oregon Health Authority last published a confirmed count of 20 cases on April 22, with no update since, despite the first Oregon hospitalization on May 12 (patient discharged, recovering), active Washington State outbreak (40+ cases, 8 counties, Kittitas County active), and a national CDC count of 1,893 as of May 14. The school vaccination window is approximately 7 days — two days closer to closure from the May 20 estimate. The Memorial Day extended weekend (May 22-26) consumes roughly half of the remaining school window without the institutional speed or scale of in-session school operations. After the school year ends, the intervention channel shifts permanently to outpatient and community health settings, which cannot replicate the speed or coverage of a school-based vaccination campaign. Any new county outbreak declaration, new Oregon hospitalization, or school-exposure event in this 7-day window represents a critical escalation. Third: Portland's $172 million city budget shortfall continues to compound under Hormuz energy costs (gas above $5.30/gallon), 30-year Treasury above 5% (municipal borrowing cost pressure), and state revenue compression from the supply-shock economic slowdown.
actors: OHA State Health Officer Dean Sidelinger

items.headline: Oregon Fire Day 15 / WA Fourth Drought Year: 10 Days to East Cascades Onset; 82% Drought Statewide; Southern Cascades Extreme; ECMWF -3.98 Inch Anomaly; Prepositioning Window 10 Days — Recess Closes Federal Channels
items.summary: Pacific Northwest fire and drought conditions advance to the most acute structural configuration of the season on Friday May 22. Oregon fire season is Day 15; the east Cascades above-normal fire onset threshold is 10 days out (June 1, NIFC); BLM full fire restrictions for Oregon and Washington are Day 9 (effective May 14). The federal prepositioning window has consumed 15 days since Oregon's congressional Democrats sent their May 7 letter flagging Forest Service Region 6 capacity deficits — from DOGE-related elimination of 1,400+ certified firefighter-eligible employees, $0 forest research funding, and a planned 20% staff reduction — with no confirmed federal response. The Memorial Day recess closes federal legislative channels and reduces agency staffing levels through May 26, consuming 4 of the remaining 10 prepositioning days without a federal response path available. When Congress returns on May 26, 6 days will remain until the June 1 onset threshold. Oregon statewide drought coverage has expanded to 82%. The Southern Cascades — the mountain corridor providing fuel moisture and fire behavior context for the state's highest-risk east-slope terrain — have reached 'extreme' drought, a designation rare for late May and indicating the most severe soil moisture deficit at fire-season entry in the current cycle. The ECMWF seasonal model projects the combined heat and drought signal to persist through July for the Pacific Coast corridor, with a -3.98-inch precipitation anomaly over the three-month window. AccuWeather projects 5.5-8 million national acres burned in 2026 — above 2025's 5.13 million. Washington State remains in a statewide drought emergency for the fourth consecutive year: 12+ days without measurable rain at Sea-Tac; eastern Washington in moderate drought per the US Drought Monitor; snowpack at approximately 50% of normal; above-normal fire risk projected east of the Cascades by June. Columbia Basin agricultural irrigation operations are under acute stress. The Pine Mountain Fire (Central Oregon, 2,589 acres) was at 85%+ containment as of the prior brief. National YTD acreage burned stands at approximately 1.85 million acres — nearly double the 10-year average — signaling elevated national aerial and ground resource demand before the West's peak season begins. Each day without federal prepositioning action is an irreversible reduction of the response capacity window.

items.headline: OHA Measles 30 Days Stale — School Window ~7 Days, Memorial Day Weekend Consumes 4; WA Kittitas Active; Gas >$5.30 OR / >$5.71 WA; Brent $106.92; Portland $172M Shortfall
items.summary: Four PNW secondary threads. First: OHA measles enters 30 days of publication staleness on Friday May 22. Oregon Health Authority last published 20 confirmed cases on April 22 with no update since, despite the first Oregon hospitalization (May 12, patient discharged, recovering), ongoing Washington State outbreak (40+ cases, 8 counties, Kittitas County in active outbreak status), and a national CDC count of 1,893 as of May 14. State epidemiologist Dr. Dean Sidelinger has stated that the 20 reported cases represent 'just the tip of the iceberg,' with many patients managing illness at home. The school vaccination window is approximately 7 days — but the Memorial Day extended weekend (May 22-26) effectively consumes 4 of those 7 remaining days without institutional school channel velocity. After the school year ends, the intervention channel shifts permanently to outpatient and community health settings, which cannot replicate the scale or organizational speed of a school-based vaccination campaign. The school window is approaching the logistical threshold below which emergency school-based vaccination mobilization becomes non-viable. Any new county outbreak declaration, new Oregon hospitalization, or documented school-exposure event in this window is a critical escalation signal. Second: Portland-metro gasoline holds above $5.30/gallon; Washington State holds above $5.71/gallon. Brent crude at approximately $106.92 and WTI at approximately $100.59 sustain the Hormuz-driven energy cost floor across PNW retail markets. Trump's 'willing to wait a few days' patience signal does not constitute near-term pump relief — even a confirmed deal framework with Hormuz reopening language would require weeks of implementation before retail fuel prices respond. Third: Washington State's fourth consecutive drought emergency compounds PNW agricultural export exposure; the Columbia Basin's contribution to Pacific Northwest wheat, apple, hop, and tree-fruit production is under acute irrigation water stress heading into the growing season. Fourth: Portland's $172 million city budget shortfall compounds under Hormuz energy costs, the 30-year Treasury at 5.18% raising municipal borrowing costs, and state revenue compression from the supply-shock economic slowdown. Memorial Day recess closes the federal legislative response window through May 26.

analyst_summary: Friday May 22, 2026 morning — Hormuz Day 84, Naval Blockade Day 41, Project Freedom Pause Day 17, WPA Day 23 Past Statutory Deadline / 7 Days to 90-Day Hard Deadline May 29, Warsh Day 8. Vibe 3. The overnight period delivers two structurally significant developments and extends the accountability gap on one critical domestic thread. The primary domestic development: House Republican leadership canceled the scheduled Iran war powers resolution vote on the afternoon of May 21, after a procedural signal on an unrelated bill revealed eight Republican absences and six Republicans voting with Democrats — a majority coalition that Rep. Golden's confirmed flip to yes made operationally complete. Rep. Meeks: 'No question about it, we would have succeeded.' The cancellation defers the next House attempt to early June, after the Memorial Day recess and after the WPA 90-day hard deadline on May 29. The bipartisan coalition against unauthorized war is now demonstrably majority-capable in the House. The May 29 deadline arrives in a recess period with no vote scheduled; the legal architecture changes fundamentally at Day 90 — the administration's 'hostilities terminated' posture does not survive plain-text scrutiny of the 90-day provision. The primary geopolitical development: third-party reporting has established for the first time that the actual enrichment moratorium negotiating range is 12-15 years — a 3-year margin rather than the 15-year gap implied by public framing. This is the most significant structural convergence on the primary nuclear sticking point since the Axios MOU scoop of May 6. It does not resolve the categorical gap between Witkoff's dismantlement demand and any moratorium-based framework, nor does it satisfy the congressional zero-enrichment constraint — but it establishes that serious negotiating positions exist in the middle ground, and that prior 'unbridgeable gap' characterizations reflected posturing. Pakistan's Army Chief is traveling to Tehran, representing the most substantive mediation escalation since Vance's Islamabad visit. Trump signals patience. The 30-year Treasury has hit 5.18%, the highest since 2007; Warsh is Day 8 without a statement; US News published this morning: 'Warsh Takes Over Fed With a Policy Problem Already in View.' Memorial Day recess begins today through May 26, closing federal legislative channels one day before the WPA 90-day deadline. Oregon fire season is Day 15 with 10 days to east Cascades onset; 82% of the state is in drought with the Southern Cascades at extreme; the ECMWF projects -3.98 inches through July; the federal prepositioning window is 10 days and the delegation letter has been unanswered 15 days; the recess closes 4 of the remaining 10 prepositioning days. OHA measles is 30 days stale with 7 days left in the school window, and the Memorial Day weekend consumes 4 of those 7 days without school operations. Vibe 3: the deal track has structural convergence; the constitutional clock is running; the fire season entry conditions are the worst of the current cycle; every calendar-driven negative is working against every structural positive. Vibe 3 is a holding pattern with elevated downside risk on multiple vectors.
watch_items: May 29 — WPA 90-Day Hard Deadline: the most consequential domestic constitutional milestone of the conflict cycle; war operates on executive fiat alone beyond any credible statutory theory; monitor for any administration legal statement at Day 90, emergency congressional action before the deadline, or acceleration of the supplemental appropriations timeline; recess makes pre-deadline legislative action structurally non-viable

Witkoff dismantlement vs. moratorium distinction: the most important analytical question of the current deal track — the reported 12-15-year moratorium negotiating range is categorically distinct from Witkoff's public dismantlement demand (Natanz, Fordow, Isfahan); any official US statement clarifying whether dismantlement or moratorium is the operative US position is the highest-priority geopolitical signal of the morning
